items.headline: Nvidia weighs $10bn anchor stake as Anthropic nears $2tn, mid-October Nasdaq listing
items.note: Nvidia is reportedly in talks to commit up to $10bn as anchor investor; Anthropic's IPO could raise up to $100bn at a roughly $2tn valuation (versus a $965bn private mark in May), with a Nasdaq landing targeted for mid-October 2026 — this is the exact trigger named in the queue. Corroborated by a 7 October search snapshot citing NYT reporting on the same $100bn/$2tn figures, so the story is still live this week even though the verified article is dated 15 September.

items.headline: JPMorgan and Citi confirm Q3 results on 13 October, setting up a direct comparison
items.note: Consensus pegs JPMorgan Q3 revenue at $50,847m and EPS at $5.86, against a raised FY2026 guide (total NII ~$105.5bn, adjusted expense ~$107.5bn). Citi reports the same day. Results land six days from today — inside the mid-October trigger window.

items.headline: Claude Haiku 4.5's retirement window opens 15 October
items.note: Anthropic's own lifecycle table lists claude-haiku-4-5 as 'not sooner than 15 October 2026' — tentative, no formal deprecation notice issued yet, so this is a primary-source date rather than a breaking story, but it crosses into a one-week window as of today.

items.headline: Nvidia's $600bn backstop turns chip vendor into AI's de facto central bank
items.note: Breaks Nvidia's OpenAI exposure into a $250bn Ohio data-centre financing guarantee, $350bn in proposed chip financing and a $30bn direct stake; argues OpenAI's creditworthiness is effectively borrowed from its own supplier. Running narrative rather than a fresh news hook — dated late July.

items.headline: Burry's $176bn depreciation gap resurfaces ahead of hyperscaler Q3 earnings
items.note: Burry's claim: hyperscalers depreciate GPUs over five-to-six years against a real two-to-three-year life, overstating 2026–28 profit by roughly $176bn, with Oracle (~27%) and Meta (~21%) singled out. Flagging only as background for this essay's actual trigger — late-October hyperscaler earnings — since the underlying story is eleven months old, not a fresh 24-hour hook.

items.headline: Verification eats 60% of enterprise agentic AI spend, McKinsey finds
items.note: McKinsey: 60% of agentic AI spend goes to response refinement/checking; enterprise AI users average $14,200 a year each in verification time ($2.84m for a 500-person firm with 200 users); Forrester estimates ungoverned generative-AI use will cost B2B firms over $10bn. Trade-press sourced rather than FT/WSJ, and dated mid-June, so treat as a numbers reservoir rather than a breaking hook.
